title: Overview
summary: Fast, flexible AI guardrails powered by Jev decisions.
text:
Fast, flexible AI guardrails Guardrails at the  speed of a decision. Jev turns complex state into typed answers without generating pages of text. Juardrails combines them into auditable policy decisions for agent tools, application actions, and your own risks—using one provider call per policy evaluation. Install Juardrails  → Why Jev is different ↗ TypeSafe reports 70–500 ms provider responses in its published examples.  Read the evidence and limits → One request · multiple risk checks ⌘ Incoming action Claude Code · Bash tool call ◇ Jev evaluation Typed answers in parallel ✓ Policy result Only allow moves forward ALLOW One call → answers → decision → audit 
 Fast by design Parallel Jev answers, one provider request per policy Broader scope Write policy questions for risks beyond prompt injection Cost conscious Typed decisions instead of generated LLM responses 
 Why this matters One guardrail system for many decisions A prompt-injection detector recognizes a defined set of attacks. Juardrails can also check destructive tool use, secret exposure, unsafe external actions, and rules specific to your workflow. In TypeSafe's published workflow evaluations, Jev sits on a strong accuracy, speed, and cost frontier against the LLM configurations tested. Explore the comparison and sources → Purpose-built decision model Jev + your policy 01  Ask typed questions 02  Apply your thresholds 03  Enforce the result 
 Find your path Everything you need to ship guardrails From a first policy to agent tool interception, each guide focuses on one working flow. 
 ↓ Install one binary Get the server, Web UI, and CLI in one verified download for your OS. Choose your platform → ↗ Get started Bootstrap the server and make your first decision. Start the walkthrough → ▣ Use the Web UI See screenshots of policy authoring, evaluation, history, and access. Explore the interface → ◇ Design a policy Understand Choice, Score, Noul, thresholds, and decision modes. Learn the model → ⌘ Secure Claude Code Install a policy pack with a pre-tool hook and reusable skills. See the pack → ›_ Work from the CLI Apply, explain, simulate, evaluate, and administer with one interface. Explore commands → ⊞ Control access Give each service account only the namespace actions it needs. Review permissions → 
 One integration surface A small system with a clear boundary Juardrails answers a focused question: should this action proceed under this policy? Your application or harness enforces the returned decision. The server keeps policy versions and evaluation traces; its authorization layer checks every request. Explore the REST API → tool call
    ↓
service account + namespace grant
    ↓
active policy + Jev evaluation
    ↓
allow | block | review | error
    ↓
your app enforces the result

title: Why Jev
summary: Why typed Jev decisions make practical guardrails fast, flexible, and cost efficient.
text:
Why Juardrails · Decision speed 
 Fast decisions, broad guardrails 
 A guardrail runs in the path of an action. Jev is built for typed decisions instead of generated prose, and Juardrails turns those answers into an explicit  allow ,  block ,  review , or  error  decision. 
 
   70–500 ms TypeSafe-reported Jev provider response range for its published examples 
   1 request Juardrails batches every criterion in a policy into one Jev call 
   Typed answers Choice, Score, and Noul values feed deterministic policy rules 
 
 The timing above is  TypeSafe's published provider figure , not a Juardrails end-to-end benchmark. Your result includes network, authorization, provider queueing, policy evaluation, and audit writes. Measure it in your deployment. 

 Why the decision path can be fast 
 Jev returns probabilities for structured questions in parallel rather than generating an explanatory answer token by token. Juardrails sends all policy questions with the input state in a single provider request, validates the typed answers, and combines them with  all ,  any , or  weighted  rules in Go. The caller receives a compact decision it can enforce immediately. 
 Your action Tool call, message, document, or agent trace → One Jev call Parallel typed answers for every criterion → Policy decision Thresholds, review gates, and audit 
 TypeSafe's  published workflow evaluations  report that decomposed decision workflows are more accurate, faster, and cheaper than asking the tested models to solve the same task in one prompt. Jev sits on a strong accuracy, latency, and cost frontier against the LLM configurations in those tests. These are provider-run evaluations across four automation workflows; they do not establish a speedup or accuracy rate for every Juardrails policy. 

 Beyond a single threat detector 
 A purpose-built prompt-injection model can be valuable for that one job. For example,  Meta's Prompt Guard model card  describes three output labels: benign, injection, and jailbreak. Those labels do not answer whether a proposed shell command is destructive, a tool call exposes a secret, an invoice meets an approval rule, or an agent response violates your own policy. 
 Juardrails lets you define those questions in YAML and combine them under one policy. You can change the rubric and thresholds without training a new classifier, and use the same service for different applications and agent harnesses. 
 Approach What it is suited to What you must design 
 Prompt-injection classifier Detecting the attack classes in its model card Additional controls for other risks and actions 
 General LLM judge Open-ended interpretation and explanations Prompting, output parsing, latency and cost controls 
 Juardrails + Jev Configurable, typed decisions across many policy questions Clear criteria, thresholds, testing, and enforcement by your caller 
 
 Flexible scope is not a universal accuracy claim A specialized detector may outperform a general policy on its own benchmark. Juardrails has no published head-to-head accuracy test against prompt-injection models. Evaluate each policy on representative allowed and disallowed cases, review false positives and false negatives, and tune its thresholds before enforcing it. 

 Cost and accuracy in practice 
 Jev's typed outputs and parallel sampling are the basis of TypeSafe's reported cost advantage over LLM-based decision workflows. Its  September 2026 analysis  describes the workload, comparison models, and important caveats. Juardrails also reduces repeated provider round trips by batching a policy's questions. The final bill depends on your provider, input size, number of calls, and current pricing. 
 Accuracy depends on the question and policy design. Noul returns a yes probability; Choice and Score provide distributions and confidence. Juardrails can route low-confidence answers to  review , while explicit thresholds turn the rest into stable decision rules. That gives teams a way to calibrate for their own risks instead of relying on a single opaque safe/unsafe label. 

 Measure your own guardrail path 
 Run live evaluations with representative inputs and record p50 and p95 time from your caller, the returned decision, and provider token usage in  juardrails cli history . Measure the whole path with the service in its intended region. Include allowed, blocked, and borderline cases; a fast decision is useful only when its error rate is acceptable for your workflow. 
 juardrails cli evaluate claude-code-tool-use sample-tool-call.json
juardrails cli history claude-code-tool-use 
 See  policy design  for typed criteria and  the Claude Code pack  for a working multi-risk policy.

title: Install
summary: Install one Juardrails executable for macOS, Linux, or Windows.
text:
Essentials · Distribution Install one executable A Juardrails release contains one self-contained executable for your operating system and CPU. The same file starts the server, bootstraps its administrator, and runs the service-account CLI. You do not need Go, Node.js, or a separate CLI download. 
 Quick install macOS or Linux Download the installer, inspect it if you wish, then run it. It verifies the release binary against  SHA256SUMS  and installs to  ~/.local/bin . curl -fL https://github.com/abhaybhargav/juardrails/releases/latest/download/install.sh -o install-juardrails.sh
sh install-juardrails.sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
~/.local/bin/juardrails version Windows PowerShell The installer checks the release SHA-256 and copies  juardrails.exe  to your local app data directory. Invoke-WebRequest https://github.com/abhaybhargav/juardrails/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile install-juardrails.ps1
.\install-juardrails.ps1
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Juardrails\bin\juardrails.exe" version 
 The installers resolve the latest release to one exact version, verify its checksum, print the destination, and tell you if it needs to be added to  PATH . Set  JUARDRAILS_VERSION=v0.1.3  to pin a release, or  JUARDRAILS_INSTALL_DIR  to choose another directory. On PowerShell, set these as environment variables before running the script. 
 Manual download Choose one file from  the latest GitHub release , verify it with the release's  SHA256SUMS , rename it to  juardrails  (or  juardrails.exe  on Windows), and place it on  PATH . System Release asset Linux x86-64 juardrails-linux-amd64 Linux ARM64 juardrails-linux-arm64 macOS Intel juardrails-darwin-amd64 macOS Apple Silicon juardrails-darwin-arm64 Windows x86-64 juardrails-windows-amd64.exe Windows ARM64 juardrails-windows-arm64.exe 
 First run On the server machine, bootstrap and start the service. You can create policies and simulate supplied answers without a provider key. For live evaluation, set  TYPESAFE_API_KEY  in the environment or a  .env  file before starting the server. juardrails bootstrap
juardrails
# Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 Bootstrap saves the human admin password under  data/bootstrap-admin.json  and injects a dedicated service-account token into  ~/.juardrails/credentials.json . Sign in as  admin , change the password under  Your account , then remove the bootstrap file. The  Web UI walkthrough  shows policy creation and evaluation. The CLI always reads its local service credential from that standard path; it does not accept a human session token. juardrails cli list
juardrails cli explain POLICY_ID
juardrails cli evaluate POLICY_ID state.json 
 CLI on another machine Install the same executable there and have an administrator provision a service token with only the needed namespace actions. Inject  {"url":"https://your-server","token":"jrd_..."}  into  ~/.juardrails/credentials.json . On Unix, its directory must be mode 0700 and the file mode 0600. On Windows, restrict both ACLs to your user, SYSTEM, and Administrators; the CLI checks this before use. 
 How releases are built GitHub Actions  runs the Go and policy-pack tests, cross-compiles all six targets with  CGO_ENABLED=0 , and stores build artifacts on pushes and pull requests. A version tag such as  v0.1.0  publishes those binaries and SHA-256 checksums as a GitHub release. The web UI and its assets are embedded in each executable. Continue with  Get started  for your first policy or the  CLI guide  for command details.

title: Get started
summary: Bootstrap Juardrails and make your first decision.
text:
Essentials · 5 minutes Get started Install one executable, bootstrap the first identities, and create a guardrail in the browser. The same  juardrails  file serves the Web UI and API and runs the service-account CLI. 
 Requirements Install the single release binary  for your OS, or build from source with Go 1.26+. Live evaluation needs a configured TypeSafe Jev key or another supported Jev provider; simulation does not. 
 Bootstrap the server Install the executable Use the  release installer  for macOS, Linux, or Windows. Add its install directory to  PATH  if needed. Create the initial identities Run  juardrails bootstrap . It creates the permanent human super-admin and a dedicated  cli-admin  service account. Start the server Run  juardrails  and open  http://127.0.0.1:8080 . Keep it running while using the browser or CLI. 
 juardrails version
juardrails bootstrap
juardrails 
 The generated human admin password is stored at  data/bootstrap-admin.json  with private permissions. Sign in as  admin , change the password under  Your account , then remove that bootstrap file. The CLI credential is stored separately at  ~/.juardrails/credentials.json  in a private directory. Bootstrap refuses to overwrite it. 
 Create and test in the Web UI Open  Policies → Create policy . Add typed questions and thresholds in the visual builder, choose  Validate , then  Save policy . Open  Playground  to simulate supplied answers while the policy is a draft. The  illustrated Web UI walkthrough  shows every step, including live Jev evaluation, history, and access control. 
 The policy library is the starting point for browser authoring. 
 Optional: load the example with the CLI The included support-safety policy is a draft, so you can inspect and simulate it immediately. The CLI uses the local service-account credential created by bootstrap. The example simulation supplies Jev answers explicitly and does not call a provider. 
 curl -fL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhaybhargav/juardrails/main/examples/support-safety.yaml -o support-safety.yaml
curl -fL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhaybhargav/juardrails/main/examples/simulation.json -o simulation.json
juardrails cli apply support-safety.yaml
juardrails cli list
juardrails cli explain support-safety
juardrails cli simulate support-safety simulation.json 
 The example files are in the repository; on Windows, download them from  the examples directory  or supply your own policy and state files. To change a policy, edit its YAML, run  juardrails cli validate FILE , then  juardrails cli apply FILE . On update, the CLI uses the current server version unless the file supplies an explicit version. Every save creates a revision. 
 Enable live evaluation Put  TYPESAFE_API_KEY  in the server's  .env  file or environment and restart the server. Set the policy status to  active . Then pass a JSON state file to  evaluate : 
 curl -fL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhaybhargav/juardrails/main/examples/state.json -o state.json
juardrails cli evaluate support-safety state.json 
 Decisions are not enforcement Only  decision: "allow"  is an allow. Your application must handle  block ,  review ,  error , failed requests, and transport errors before acting. 
 Where to go next Web UI Follow the  screenshot walkthrough  to author, simulate, evaluate, and inspect a decision. Policy model Use the  policy guide  to choose question types and decision modes. Agent tools Install the  Claude Code pack  to screen tool calls with this server.

title: Web UI walkthrough
summary: Create, test, inspect, and administer guardrails in the browser.
text:
Essentials · Browser walkthrough Use the Web UI The single  juardrails  executable serves the Web UI, API, and CLI. In the browser, you can create a policy, test its decision logic, run a live Jev evaluation, inspect the trace, and manage access. 
 Start here Install the release binary , run  juardrails bootstrap , then start  juardrails . Open  http://127.0.0.1:8080  and sign in as  admin  with the generated password in  data/bootstrap-admin.json . If you set  JUARDRAILS_ADMIN_USER  and  JUARDRAILS_ADMIN_PASSWORD  before bootstrap, use those instead. Change the initial password under  Your account  and remove the bootstrap file. 
 The screenshots below come from an isolated demo workspace. They show actual screens and results, including a supplied-answer simulation and one live provider request. The example policy and input are illustrative. 
 1. Find or create a policy Open  Policies . The library shows each policy's status, question types, decision mode, and revision. Search or filter by status, then choose  Create policy  or open an existing row. The namespace selector in the sidebar controls which policies you see. 
 Policy library in the root namespace. The sample has two Noul criteria and requires both to pass. 
 2. Define typed questions and pass rules In  Visual builder , enter a stable policy ID, name, description, status, and model. Add one focused criterion per question. Choose  Noul  for a yes/no probability,  Choice  for named outcomes, or  Score  for an ordered rubric. Set the pass condition and choose whether all, any, or a weighted fraction must pass. Use  Validate  before  Save policy . The  YAML policy  tab lets you edit or import the same definition as code, and  Export  downloads it. Saving an existing policy creates a new revision. 
 The visual editor identifies the policy and keeps draft and active status explicit. 
 Each criterion has its own question, probability anchors, threshold, and weight. 
 3. Simulate before using a provider Open  Playground , select a draft or active policy, and keep  Simulation · supplied answers  selected. Enter representative state and edit the generated typed-answer fixture to test passing, failing, and borderline cases. Choose  Run simulation  to see the decision and each criterion's result. Simulation checks the decision rules against your answers; it does not ask Jev to judge the state. 
 This supplied-answer simulation blocks because the instruction override probability exceeds its 0.2 pass threshold. 
 4. Evaluate an active policy with Jev Change the policy status to  Active — live evaluation enabled  and save it. Configure a Jev provider key on the server, then select  Live · Jev API  in Playground. Enter text or structured JSON and choose  Evaluate with Jev . The server sends the state to the configured provider and combines the typed answers under the saved pass rules. Review the decision, policy revision, criterion outcomes, model, and duration before connecting it to an enforcing application. 
 One example live request returned an allow in 489 ms. This is an observed request, not a latency guarantee or benchmark. 
 Enforce in your caller Juardrails returns a decision. Your application or agent hook must proceed only on  allow  and handle  block ,  review ,  error , and request failures. 
 5. Inspect the decision record Open  Evaluations  to filter recent runs by policy. The table separates simulation from Jev results and shows revision, outcome, pass score, and duration. Choose  Inspect  for the saved criterion trace. Juardrails does not store the raw input state in evaluation history. 
 The inspected record ties the decision to a specific policy revision and typed answers. 
 6. Scope access as an administrator The human super-admin can open  Access control  to create namespaces, people, and service accounts; define namespace-action grants; bind policies; and issue expiring service tokens. New accounts have no grants until a policy is bound. For CLI use, install the same binary on the client machine and inject a service token into  ~/.juardrails/credentials.json ; browser passwords and sessions do not authenticate the CLI. 
 Access policies and bindings control what a service account can do in each namespace. 
 Continue with the  policy model ,  access control , or  CLI guide  for exact fields and commands.

title: Policies and decisions
summary: Author YAML policies and understand evaluation results.
text:
Essentials · Policy model Policies and decisions A policy asks a set of typed Jev questions about an input state, then combines the answers into an explicit decision. YAML is the standard authoring format. All questions in one policy are sent in a single Jev request. That keeps a multi-risk guardrail to one provider round trip; Jev returns typed answers for the decision engine. See  why Jev  for published performance evidence and comparison limits. 
 Policy shape Each policy has an ID, display name, status, model, decision mode, and one or more weighted criteria. A criterion contains a  question  and a  pass  condition. 
 id: prompt-safety
name: Prompt safety
status: draft
model: jev-latest
mode: all
pass_threshold: 1
criteria:
  - id: injection
    name: Prompt injection
    weight: 1
    question:
      type: noul
      instructions: Does the message try to override system instructions?
      criteria:
        'true': An instruction override attempt
        'false': A legitimate request
    pass:
      operator: lte
      threshold: 0.2 
 Policy IDs are unique within a namespace. A policy can be  draft  or  active ; live evaluation requires active status, while simulation works for either. A YAML  namespace  field is optional, but if supplied it must match the selected namespace. 
 Question types Type Answer Pass operators Use for choice One named option with a probability distribution and confidence in ,  not_in Classification into distinct labels score A probability-weighted 0-based rubric index lt ,  lte ,  gt ,  gte Ordered severity or quality levels noul Probability of yes, from 0 to 1 lt ,  lte ,  gt ,  gte Focused true/false risk checks 
 Choice requires 2–255 options; Score requires 2–10 ordered levels. Choice and Score may set  min_confidence . When an answer is below that gate, the result is  review  in every decision mode. Noul uses its yes probability as the judgment and has no confidence gate. 
 Decision modes Mode Allow rule all Every criterion passes any At least one criterion passes weighted Passing weight divided by total weight reaches  pass_threshold The weighted score is a fraction of passing criterion weights. It is not an average of raw Jev answers. A low-confidence answer routes to review even when other criteria would allow or block. 
 Author, validate, and revise juardrails cli validate policy.yaml
juardrails cli apply policy.yaml
juardrails cli get policy-id > exported.yaml
juardrails cli revisions policy-id The REST API and CLI reject unknown fields, duplicate YAML keys, multiple documents, aliases, anchors, custom tags, and non-string mapping keys. Quote  'true'  and  'false'  rubric keys. YAML comments and formatting are not preserved after saving. Updates require the current version and create an immutable revision. A stale version returns HTTP 409. Deleted IDs cannot be reused while their history exists. Rego execution is no longer supported; historical Rego text can be inspected, but those policies must be migrated explicitly to a supported mode. 
 Live evaluations and simulations evaluate  sends the state and all questions to the configured Jev provider, validates the provider's complete typed answer map, runs the decision engine, and records the result.  simulate  accepts supplied answers and uses the same answer validator and decision engine without contacting Jev. 
 juardrails cli evaluate policy-id state.json
juardrails cli simulate policy-id simulation.json
juardrails cli history policy-id Interpret the whole result Read  decision ,  results ,  policy_version ,  source , and any  error . A successful CLI exit means the API request completed; it does not mean the policy allowed the action.

title: CLI guide
summary: Use a local service account to work with policies and administration.
text:
Build · Command line CLI guide The  juardrails cli  command lets an authorized service account discover, author, explain, evaluate, and administer policies without handling a human session token. 
 Install the single Juardrails executable  for macOS, Linux, or Windows. Run protected commands as  juardrails cli … ; the same file also starts the server and bootstraps the first identities. 
 Service credential Every protected command reads  ~/.juardrails/credentials.json , verifies the token with  /auth/me , and requires a service-account token. The file must be regular and private, and its containing directory must be private. HTTP is accepted only for loopback server URLs; use HTTPS remotely. ~/.juardrails/                 # mode 0700
└── credentials.json          # mode 0600

{"url":"https://juardrails.example.com","token":"jrd_..."} juardrails bootstrap  creates a local CLI credential on first setup. For other machines, an administrator can issue a narrower service token and inject the file there. The CLI ignores  JUARDRAILS_TOKEN ; do not put a human session in the file. On Windows, mode bits do not describe access; the CLI checks the directory and file ACLs instead. Allow only your user, SYSTEM, and Administrators. 
 Policy commands Command Purpose juardrails cli list List policies visible in the selected namespace juardrails cli get ID  /  export ID Print normalized YAML juardrails cli explain ID Summarize criteria and pass conditions juardrails cli validate FILE Validate a YAML or JSON policy juardrails cli apply FILE Create or update a policy juardrails cli delete ID Delete the current version juardrails cli revisions ID Inspect immutable revisions juardrails cli evaluate ID FILE Run live Jev evaluation of an active policy juardrails cli simulate ID FILE Evaluate supplied answers without Jev juardrails cli history [ID] Read recent evaluation traces Use  -  as  FILE  to read JSON or YAML from stdin. Select a namespace before the command: juardrails cli -namespace engineering/production list
juardrails cli -namespace engineering/production evaluate tool-use state.json 
 Administrator commands The CLI can administer only when its service account has an explicit global  admin:manage  grant. The bootstrap CLI account has that grant; ordinary service accounts do not. juardrails cli admin users list
juardrails cli admin users get ID
juardrails cli admin users create user.json
juardrails cli admin users update ID changes.json
juardrails cli admin users delete ID
juardrails cli admin users password ID password.json
juardrails cli admin users get-bindings ID
juardrails cli admin users bindings ID bindings.json

juardrails cli admin access list
juardrails cli admin access get NAME
juardrails cli admin access create grants.yaml
juardrails cli admin access update grants.yaml NAME
juardrails cli admin access delete NAME
juardrails cli admin access revisions NAME

juardrails cli admin tokens list
juardrails cli admin tokens create token.json
juardrails cli admin tokens revoke ID
juardrails cli admin namespaces list
juardrails cli admin namespaces create namespace.json
juardrails cli admin namespaces update namespace.json
juardrails cli admin auth-settings get
juardrails cli admin auth-settings set settings.json Admin user, token, namespace, and settings files are JSON; access-policy files may be YAML or JSON.  juardrails cli request METHOD /path [FILE|-]  exposes advanced  /api/v1  endpoints through the same service credential. 
 Use decisions in scripts Never equate exit code 0 with an allow. A successful request can return  block ,  review , or  error . Parse the JSON decision and handle all other outcomes conservatively. juardrails cli evaluate tool-use state.json | jq -e '.decision == "allow"' Protect local inputs too The service does not store raw evaluation state, but live evaluation sends it to the configured Jev provider. Avoid putting secrets in state unless that data flow is permitted for your deployment.

title: Access control
summary: Namespaces, service accounts, grants, tokens, and admin operations.
text:
Build · Authorization Access control Juardrails separates the policies that make decisions from access policies that decide who may work with them. Every request is authenticated and checked against namespace grants. 
 Human and service identities The permanent human super-admin is created once during bootstrap and can use the browser access page. Other humans sign in with passwords. Service accounts have no passwords; an administrator issues them expiring tokens. Every non-admin account starts with no grants. Humans Browser sessions use an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie. Cookie-authenticated writes need a CSRF token. Services Use an opaque bearer token. The CLI accepts only service tokens from its private credential file. 
 Service tokens require an expiry no more than 365 days ahead. Secrets are shown once at creation; token metadata can be listed and tokens revoked. Disabling an account revokes its tokens. The human super-admin cannot be disabled or deleted. 
 Namespaces The default namespace is  root . Names such as  engineering/production  provide separate policy IDs, revisions, and evaluation history. Parents must exist before nested namespaces are created. Namespace names are retained to preserve historical references. REST clients send  X-Juardrails-Namespace ; CLI clients use  -namespace NAME  or  JUARDRAILS_NAMESPACE . Listing namespaces reveals only those for which the principal has at least one action. 
 Access policies and bindings An access policy is a collection of namespace-action rules. Bind one or more policies to a principal; grants add together, and everything else is denied. name: production-evaluator
description: Evaluate approved production guardrails
rules:
  - namespace: engineering/production
    actions:
      - policies:evaluate Selector Meaning engineering/production Exact namespace only engineering/** Engineering and all descendants * Every namespace Exact namespace rules do not inherit to descendants. Grants are checked on every request, so binding changes affect the next request. An evaluation already in progress completes under its original authorization. 
 Actions Action Allows policies:read List, get, and inspect policy revisions policies:create Create policies and validate new documents policies:update Update existing policies and validate documents policies:delete Delete current policies policies:evaluate Evaluate a known active policy ID policies:simulate Simulate supplied answers evaluations:read Read evaluation history admin:manage Manage identities, grants, tokens, namespaces, and auth settings through the API admin:manage  is special: it requires an explicit rule with namespace  *  bound to a service account. A wildcard action does not imply it. The browser access page remains restricted to the human super-admin. 
 Design a narrow service account Create a service principal Use the access page or  juardrails cli admin users create  while signed in as an administrator. Bind only required actions For an app that evaluates one known policy,  policies:evaluate  in one namespace is enough. Issue and inject the token Set an expiry, store the returned secret once in a protected credential file, and plan rotation before it expires. 
 The Web UI binds explicit namespace grants to service accounts. New accounts have no access until a policy is bound. See the  Web UI walkthrough  for the complete browser flow.

title: REST API
summary: Endpoints, versioning, authentication, and response handling.
text:
Build · HTTP interface REST API The API is the shared surface for the browser, CLI, and applications. All application routes use  /api/v1 ; only process health and password login are unauthenticated. 
 Request basics Use  Authorization: Bearer TOKEN  for service and REST clients. The optional  X-Juardrails-Namespace  header defaults to  root . Policy writes accept YAML or JSON; other bodies require JSON. Request bodies are limited to 1 MiB and reject unknown fields. curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/v1/policies \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_TOKEN" \
  -H 'X-Juardrails-Namespace: root' Get the exact machine-readable contract from the running server at  /api/v1/openapi.json , or  inspect it in the repository ↗ . 
 Policy endpoints Method Path Purpose GET / POST /policies List / create GET / PUT / DELETE /policies/{id} Read / update / delete POST /policies/validate Validate a policy document GET /policies/{id}/revisions Immutable revisions POST /policies/{id}/evaluate Live evaluation POST /policies/{id}/simulate Supplied-answer simulation GET /evaluations ,  /evaluations/{id} History and full trace 
 For YAML output, set  Accept: application/yaml  or  ?format=yaml . A PUT must include the current  version ; DELETE requires  ?version=N . A stale version returns 409. Restore an old revision by PUTting its content with the current version to create a new revision. 
 Evaluation contract POST /api/v1/policies/{id}/evaluate
Content-Type: application/json

{"state":{"message":"Please summarize this note."}} Simulations add an  answers  map with a typed answer for every criterion. Live evaluation accepts only state and requires an active policy and configured provider. A response includes  decision ,  score , per-criterion  results , source, policy version, model, timing, and any error. Use only  allow  to authorize your action. 
 Identity and administration Method Path Purpose POST /auth/login Password login for humans GET /auth/me Principal, token kind, expiry, CSRF token POST /auth/logout ,  /auth/password Revoke session / change password GET / POST / PUT /namespaces Discover / create / update namespaces GET / POST /admin/principals List / create identities GET / PUT / DELETE /admin/principals/{id} Read / update / delete a non-admin identity GET / PUT /admin/principals/{id}/bindings Read / replace grants GET / POST / PUT / DELETE /admin/access-policies  and  /{name} Manage access policies GET / POST / DELETE /admin/tokens  and  /{id} Issue / list / revoke tokens GET / PUT /admin/auth-settings Inspect / update supported auth settings Admin routes require the human super-admin or a service account with explicit global  admin:manage . Browser cookie writes also require  X-CSRF-Token . The full OpenAPI document includes exact schemas and responses. 
 Failure handling Handle 401 authentication failures, 403 denied actions, 404 missing resources or namespaces, 409 version conflicts, 422 validation failures, 429 capacity or rate limits, and 503 audit/provider availability separately. When an audit completion write fails after a mutation, the API may return 503 even if the operation committed: inspect state before retrying.

title: Claude Code pack
summary: Screen tool calls with a policy, hook, and agent skills.
text:
Integrations · Policy pack Secure Claude Code tool calls The Claude Code pack combines one active Juardrails policy, a project-scoped  PreToolUse  hook, and two agent skills. The hook screens a proposed action before Claude Code runs it. 
 Claude proposes a tool call Bash, Edit, MCP, and other matched tools → Hook calls  juardrails cli evaluate Service account from the local credential file → Policy returns a decision Only allow passes to normal permissions 
 What the policy checks The  claude-code-tool-use  policy uses three Noul risk questions in  all  mode. A tool call must pass all three. Criterion Default maximum risk Examples Destructive change 0.20 Recursive deletion, overwriting substantial data, disabling controls Secret exposure 0.40 Posting credentials or sensitive data to another destination Unsafe external action 0.20 Publishing, deployment, remote changes, executing untrusted code The hook also rejects obvious credential references locally before sending a call to the provider. This catches common token patterns and secret paths; it is not a complete secret scanner. The policy is a starting point, so calibrate it with examples from your own workflows. 
 The three questions share one Jev provider request. This makes the pack a practical example of guarding several risks without chaining three model calls. Read  why Jev  for published performance evidence; actual hook latency includes CLI, server, network, and provider time. 
 Install the pack Prepare Juardrails Install the release binary  and start a server with a Jev provider. Provision a service credential with policy read, create, update, and evaluate actions in the intended namespace. Get the pack files Clone or download the repository to obtain the policy, hook, skills, and Python installer. The release binary itself has no Go or Node dependency. Install into one project Run the installer below. It applies the policy, copies the hook and skills, and merges project  .claude/settings.json  without discarding existing settings. 
 python3 policy_packs/claude-code/install.py /path/to/claude-project \
  --juard "$(command -v juardrails)"

# Optional: install in a namespace other than root
python3 policy_packs/claude-code/install.py /path/to/claude-project \
  --juard "$(command -v juardrails)" --namespace engineering/production The example uses macOS/Linux shell syntax. The installer also accepts the legacy  juard  binary. The Windows release supports  juardrails.exe cli ; this project hook installer has been tested on macOS/Linux. Use  --no-apply  for an offline file install, then apply the YAML policy yourself. Use  --force  to replace differing pack files. Keep the executable at the  --juard  path for the installed hook; put it on Claude Code's  PATH  so skills can run  juardrails cli  interactively. 
 The included skills /juardrails Guides an agent to discover, explain, validate, apply, simulate, and evaluate authorized policies with the CLI. /claude-code-guardrails Explains this integration, its policy, and how to inspect decision history without bypassing a denial. The installer places both in the project’s  .claude/skills/  directory. For another harness, copy the general  Juardrails skill ↗  to that harness’s skill directory. For Codex, the conventional location is  ~/.codex/skills/juardrails/ . A skill provides guidance; enforcement requires a harness hook or equivalent tool interception. 
 Coverage and behavior The hook matches Bash, PowerShell, Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, WebSearch, and MCP tool calls. It sends the proposed input to the active policy through the service-account-backed CLI. It denies  block ,  review ,  error , malformed responses, oversized input, or service failure. An  allow  leaves Claude Code’s normal permission rules in place. juardrails cli explain claude-code-tool-use
juardrails cli history claude-code-tool-use 
 Understand the data flow and boundary Live evaluation sends proposed tool input, potentially including file content, to the configured Jev provider. The local credential check is best effort. Other tool types and actions outside Claude Code are not screened. Project hooks can be edited or disabled, and Claude Code may proceed if a hook process is killed or times out. Use managed settings and operating-system controls where a stronger enforcement boundary is required. 
 Test before rollout Try representative safe and risky calls in a disposable project. A routine listing or  go test ./...  should pass; recursive deletion or a command posting  .env  to a remote URL should not. Review the returned criterion scores and tune the policy before applying it broadly. python3 -m unittest discover -s policy_packs/claude-code/tests -v
go test ./...
juardrails cli history claude-code-tool-use See the  pack source and installer ↗  for the current implementation.

title: Operate securely
summary: Providers, deployment, audit, migration, and limits.
text:
Reference · Deployment Operate securely Juardrails stores policies and evaluations in SQLite, writes a durable audit log, and calls a configured Jev provider for live decisions. Treat it as a single-server policy service, with the surrounding application responsible for enforcement. 
 Configure a Jev provider The server loads an optional  .env  file in its working directory. Existing environment variables take precedence. Provider keys remain on the server; CLI credentials live separately in  ~/.juardrails . Setting Purpose JEV_PROVIDER typesafe  (default),  openrouter ,  requesty , or  custom TYPESAFE_API_KEY TypeSafe preset credential OPENROUTER_API_KEY OpenRouter preset credential REQUESTY_API_KEY Requesty preset credential JEV_API_KEY Explicit credential override for the selected provider JEV_ENDPOINT_URL Full custom endpoint URL JEV_API_FORMAT systemone  or  questions-chat JEV_DEFAULT_MODEL Model substituted for a policy’s  jev-latest  alias Use a versioned model ID in the policy when reproducibility matters. The actual returned model is recorded on live evaluation. These model judgments are probabilistic: calibrate questions and thresholds against representative data before enforcing them. 
 Server and deployment The installed  juardrails  executable serves the Web UI, API, and CLI. It listens on  127.0.0.1:8080  by default. Set  -addr ,  -db , and  -audit-log  to choose the listener, SQLite file, and append-only audit file. Use the same database and audit paths with  juardrails bootstrap . Put a public deployment behind HTTPS and set  JUARDRAILS_COOKIE_SECURE=true  when TLS terminates at a reverse proxy. juardrails bootstrap -db data/juardrails.sqlite -audit-log data/audit.jsonl
juardrails \
  -addr 127.0.0.1:8080 \
  -db data/juardrails.sqlite \
  -audit-log data/audit.jsonl Preserve the database and audit file across restarts. The SQLite store uses WAL and foreign keys. Stop the server before copying its database for a backup; for online backups use SQLite backup facilities rather than copying only the main file. This is a single-server deployment, not a distributed secret vault. 
 Auditing and retention The file audit log records request, authorized, and response events. It includes time, request ID, method, path, namespace, action, actor and token IDs, source IP, target, status, and duration. It excludes request and response bodies, passwords, token secrets, provider credentials, and evaluation input. Policy revisions and evaluation answers remain in SQLite. The audit file is append-only from the application and fsynced for durability. If the initial or authorization write fails, the action does not proceed. If the final completion write fails after a mutation has committed, the API returns 503; inspect current state before retrying. The database and file are not one atomic transaction. Restart after external audit-log rotation. Revisions and audit records have no automatic pruning. Policy listings are currently unpaginated; evaluation history uses a bounded  limit . Plan disk capacity and retention accordingly. 
 Migrate older data Default startup imports  data/juardrails.db  from bbolt into an empty  data/juardrails.sqlite . The source remains read-only and is retained. Stop the old server before migrating. For custom paths, use  -db destination.sqlite -migrate-bbolt source.db ; import into a nonempty destination is rejected. Rego execution has been removed. Existing  all ,  any , and  weighted  policies retain their behavior. For a historical Rego policy, explicitly remove the Rego text, choose a supported mode, adjust criteria, simulate representative cases, and save a new revision. 
 Security boundaries Authenticate and scope Use short-lived, least-privilege service tokens. Only an explicit global admin grant enables service administration. Enforce the result The API reports decisions. Your caller must treat every outcome except  allow  as non-authorizing. Protect input data Raw state is not persisted by Juardrails, but live state is sent to the selected provider. Back up and rotate Protect database, audit, and credential files; rotate service tokens before expiry.
